proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3 (coordinates: smoothness of F and the derivative DF(p), p = r₀u). Conventions: ⟨·,·⟩ is the real inner product; for a, b ∈ ℝ, (a, b) ∈ Euclid 2 is the point with coordinates a, b (Lean !₂[a, b]); F(x) := (‖x‖, arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,u⟩)), so the coordinates of F(x) are F(x)₀ = ‖x‖ and F(x)₁ = arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,u⟩); H := {x : 0 < ⟨x, u⟩}; p := r₀u.
1. H is open: it is the preimage of the open set (0, ∞) under the continuous map x ↦ ⟨x, u⟩ (isOpen_lt). Every x ∈ H is nonzero, since ⟨0, u⟩ = 0.
2. (Coordinate 0.) The norm of an inner product space is C^∞ at every nonzero point (contDiffAt_norm); by step 1 it is C¹ at every x ∈ H.
3. (Coordinate 1.) x ↦ ⟨x, e⟩ and x ↦ ⟨x, u⟩ are continuous linear, hence C^∞ (ContDiff.inner applied to contDiff_id and contDiff_const). For x ∈ H the denominator ⟨x, u⟩ is nonzero, so the quotient q(x) := ⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,u⟩ is C¹ at x (ContDiffAt.div). arctan is C^∞ on ℝ (Real.contDiff_arctan), so x ↦ arctan(q(x)) is C¹ at every x ∈ H (ContDiffAt.comp).
4. (F is C¹ on H.) A map into Euclid 2 = PiLp 2 (Fin 2 → ℝ) is C¹ on a set iff each of its two coordinate functions is (contDiffOn_piLp). By the simp identities (a, b)₀ = a and (a, b)₁ = b, the coordinates of F are the functions of steps 2 and 3, which are C¹ at each point of H, hence C¹ within H at each point of H. So F is C¹ on H. This is the first conclusion.
5. (Values at p.) ⟨p, u⟩ = r₀⟨u, u⟩ = r₀‖u‖² = r₀ > 0, so p ∈ H; ⟨p, e⟩ = r₀⟨u, e⟩ = 0; ‖p‖ = |r₀|·‖u‖ = r₀. Since H is open and F is C¹ on H, F is C¹ at p (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt) and hence differentiable at p (ContDiffAt.differentiableAt, 1 ≠ 0).
6. (Derivative of coordinate 0 at p.) x ↦ ‖x‖² has derivative h ↦ 2⟨p, h⟩ at p (hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq). Its value ‖p‖² = r₀² is nonzero, so x ↦ √(‖x‖²) has derivative h ↦ (1/(2√(‖p‖²)))·2⟨p, h⟩ at p (HasFDerivAt.sqrt). Since √(‖x‖²) = ‖x‖ for all x (Real.sqrt_sq, norm_nonneg) and √(r₀²) = r₀, this derivative is h ↦ (1/(2r₀))·2·r₀⟨u, h⟩ = ⟨u, h⟩. So x ↦ ‖x‖ has derivative h ↦ ⟨u, h⟩ (innerSL ℝ u) at p.
7. (Derivative of coordinate 1 at p.) a(x) := ⟨x, e⟩ has derivative h ↦ ⟨e, h⟩ and b(x) := ⟨x, u⟩ has derivative h ↦ ⟨u, h⟩ at p (continuous linear maps, using real_inner_comm). Since b(p) = r₀ ≠ 0, the map y ↦ y⁻¹ has derivative −(r₀²)⁻¹ at r₀ (hasDerivAt_inv), so by the chain rule x ↦ b(x)⁻¹ has derivative h ↦ −(r₀²)⁻¹⟨u, h⟩ at p (HasDerivAt.comp_hasFDerivAt). Since q(x) = a(x)·b(x)⁻¹, the product rule (HasFDerivAt.mul) gives Dq(p)h = a(p)·(−(r₀²)⁻¹⟨u, h⟩) + b(p)⁻¹⟨e, h⟩ = r₀⁻¹⟨e, h⟩, because a(p) = ⟨p, e⟩ = 0. Finally q(p) = 0/r₀ = 0, so by the chain rule for arctan (HasFDerivAt.arctan) x ↦ arctan(q(x)) has derivative h ↦ (1/(1 + 0²))·r₀⁻¹⟨e, h⟩ = r₀⁻¹⟨e, h⟩ at p.
8. (Identification of DF(p).) Let L := fderiv ℝ F p. For i ∈ {0, 1} the coordinate projection πᵢ : Euclid 2 → ℝ (EuclideanSpace.proj i) is continuous linear, so by the chain rule and step 5, πᵢ ∘ F has derivative πᵢ ∘ L at p. But πᵢ ∘ F is the i-th coordinate function of F, whose derivative at p was computed in step 6 (i = 0) and step 7 (i = 1); by uniqueness of the Fréchet derivative (HasFDerivAt.unique), π₀(L h) = ⟨u, h⟩ and π₁(L h) = r₀⁻¹⟨e, h⟩ = ⟨e, h⟩/r₀ for every h.
9. Two points of Euclid 2 with the same two coordinates are equal (extensionality over Fin 2), so L h = (⟨u, h⟩, ⟨e, h⟩/r₀) for every h ∈ ℝ^P. This is the second conclusion. ∎
key_steps: H = {⟨x,u⟩ > 0} is open and excludes 0; the norm is C¹ away from 0 and arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,u⟩) is C¹ where ⟨x,u⟩ ≠ 0, so F is C¹ on H coordinatewise (contDiffOn_piLp).
At p = r₀u: ⟨p,u⟩ = r₀, ⟨p,e⟩ = 0, ‖p‖ = r₀, and F is differentiable at p.
D‖·‖(p)h = ⟨p,h⟩/‖p‖ = ⟨u,h⟩ via √(‖x‖²) and the derivative of ‖x‖².
Product rule for ⟨x,e⟩·⟨x,u⟩⁻¹ with ⟨p,e⟩ = 0 and arctan′(0) = 1 give D(arctan∘q)(p)h = ⟨e,h⟩/r₀.
Projecting fderiv F p onto both coordinates and using uniqueness of derivatives gives DF(p)h = (⟨u,h⟩, ⟨e,h⟩/r₀).
